panels.title: Firing now
panels.description: wgfleet alerts vmalert is firing, newest first. Silences live in Alertmanager, so a silenced alert still shows here — check the silence list before chasing it.

targets.expr: 1000 * max by (severity, alertname, node, exit, check, probe, port, transport) (ALERTS_FOR_STATE{service="wgfleet"} and ignoring(alertstate) ALERTS{alertstate="firing",service="wgfleet"})

panels.title: Clients online
panels.description: Client peers with a fresh handshake on the masters' client interface. VLESS clients are not counted: their inbound keeps no handshake.

panels.title: Client traffic
panels.description: Both directions, all masters, last 5 minutes.

panels.title: Client path failing
panels.description: Probes the masters' own synthetic client fails right now (icmp, tcp/443, udp/53 through the whole path). Anything above 0 means real clients hurt.

panels.title: Nodes not Ready
panels.description: Nodes the controller does not report as Ready (Degraded, Error, Provisioning, Draining…).

panels.title: Exits carrying traffic
panels.description: Per master: exits wg-best currently balances over. 0 means that master's clients have no way out.

targets.expr: count by (node) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"} == 1) or on(node) (0 * max by (node) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"}))

panels.title: Reserve tier in use
panels.description: Per master: 1 when the primary exits are all down and wg-best fell back to the reserve tier.

panels.title: DNS SERVFAIL
panels.description: Share of the masters' blocky answers that are SERVFAIL — the clients' only resolver.

panels.title: Scanner knocks, last hour
panels.description: Packets opening a connection to the fleet from a scanner-feed network (C24Be + sngvy) in the last hour, all nodes. Dropped where the feed is enforced, only counted where it is observed. Replies to connections the fleet opened are never counted. A packet count: a scanner retrying a SYN counts again.

panels.title: Scanner knocks in this range, by node
panels.description: Interest in each server over the dashboard's time range: packets opening a connection from a scanner-feed network, most-knocked node on top. Dropped where the feed is enforced, only counted where it is observed. A packet count: a scanner retrying a SYN counts again. Source: wgfleet_fw_as_blacklist_hits_total.

panels.title: Scanner knocks per minute, by node
panels.description: Packets per minute opening a connection from a scanner-feed network, one line per node. Background is a few per minute on every node. A tall spike on one node for a few minutes is one sweep aimed at that node's address: it inflates that node's bar in "Scanner knocks in this range" without meaning steady extra interest. A step up that stays is a new, persistent source. Source: wgfleet_fw_as_blacklist_hits_total.

panels.title: Client peers online, per master
panels.description: Peers with a fresh handshake on wg0. A master dropping to 0 while the other rises is clients failing over; both dropping is an outage.

panels.title: Client traffic, per master
panels.description: Download (to clients) above the axis, upload below.

panels.title: Client DNS answers (masters)
panels.description: What the masters' blocky answers clients with, stacked.

panels.title: DNS latency p95, per node
panels.description: blocky request duration. Masters resolve for clients; exits resolve for their own egress.

panels.title: DNS failures, per node
panels.description: SERVFAIL answers plus blocky's own errors (upstream timeouts, list downloads).

panels.title: Clients by traffic in this range
panels.description: Every client with traffic in the selected range. via: master — the master's WireGuard client interface; lifeline — an exit's reserve interface (the same credential, used when the master is unreachable); VLESS — the master's VLESS inbound. WireGuard bytes are on the wire, VLESS bytes are payload without REALITY/XHTTP overhead, so a VLESS client reads a little lower for the same use. VLESS has no handshake column. Names and devices come from the controller; a peer it does not know shows as (unnamed) — normally just the master's own synthetic client (10.73.0.254), which probes the client path.

targets.expr: ((sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (increase(wgfleet_wg_peer_tx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__range]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (increase(wgfleet_vless_user_tx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__range])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", ""))) > 0) * on(peer) group_left(client, device) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end()))) or label_replace(label_replace((sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (increase(wgfleet_wg_peer_tx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__range]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (increase(wgfleet_vless_user_tx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__range])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", ""))) > 0) unless on(peer) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end())), "client", "(unnamed)", "", ""), "device", "", "", "")

((sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (increase(wgfleet_wg_peer_rx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__range]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (increase(wgfleet_vless_user_rx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__range])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", "")))) * on(peer) group_left(client, device) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end()))) or label_replace(label_replace((sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (increase(wgfleet_wg_peer_rx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__range]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (increase(wgfleet_vless_user_rx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__range])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", "")))) unless on(peer) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end())), "client", "(unnamed)", "", ""), "device", "", "", "")

((min by (node, iface, peer) (wgfleet_wg_handshake_age_seconds{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"})) * on(peer) group_left(client, device) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end()))) or label_replace(label_replace((min by (node, iface, peer) (wgfleet_wg_handshake_age_seconds{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"})) unless on(peer) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end())), "client", "(unnamed)", "", ""), "device", "", "", "")

panels.title: Busiest clients, download
panels.description: The eight clients pulling the most at each moment, by name. Same sources as the table on the left.

targets.expr: topk(8, ((8 * sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (rate(wgfleet_wg_peer_tx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (rate(wgfleet_vless_user_tx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", ""))) > 0) * on(peer) group_left(client, device) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end()))) or label_replace(label_replace((8 * sum by (node, iface, peer) ((sum by (node, iface, peer) (rate(wgfleet_wg_peer_tx_bytes{iface=~"wg0|awgl0",node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval]))) or (label_replace(label_replace(sum by (node, user) (rate(wgfleet_vless_user_tx_bytes{node=~"$node"}[$__rate_interval])), "peer", "$1", "user", "(.+)"), "iface", "vless", "", ""))) > 0) unless on(peer) max by (peer, client, device) (last_over_time(wgfleet_client_info[1d] @ end())), "client", "(unnamed)", "", ""), "device", "", "", ""))

panels.title: Exit × master, now
panels.description: carrying — wg-best balances over it; ready — in rotation, not chosen (reserve tier or not picked); held out — our multi-destination probe pulled it; OUT — mihomo's own check failed. `-reality` rows are the REALITY transport of the same exit.

targets.expr: max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}) + max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"}) - 3 * (max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_exit_held_out{node=~"$master"}) or 0 * max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}))

panels.title: Tunnels out of rotation ≥ 5 min in this range
panels.description: One row per master→exit tunnel that spent at least 5 minutes OUT or held out in the selected range — the rest are healthy and not drawn. Colour = what the tunnel was doing at that moment: green carrying traffic, blue in rotation but idle, orange pulled by our probe, red failed mihomo's check. The short blink every node shows at a rollout is filtered out.

targets.expr: label_join((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}) + max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"}) - 3 * (max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_exit_held_out{node=~"$master"}) or 0 * max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}))) and on(node, exit) (count_over_time(((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}) + max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"}) - 3 * (max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_exit_held_out{node=~"$master"}) or 0 * max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}))) < 1)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 5), "tunnel", " → ", "node", "exit") or on() (label_replace(vector(9), "tunnel", "every tunnel stayed in rotation", "", "") unless on() count(count_over_time(((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}) + max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_selected{node=~"$master"}) - 3 * (max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_exit_held_out{node=~"$master"}) or 0 * max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_exit_tunnel_alive{node=~"$master"}))) < 1)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 5))

panels.title: Traffic leaving each exit (WARP)
panels.description: Both directions on each exit's WARP interface — client traffic from every master and every transport, plus the agent's own probes (~10 KB/s). An exit on direct egress is absent here.

panels.title: Tunnel delay, worst master per exit (5 min avg)
panels.description: mihomo's url-test delay through each exit, the slower of the masters, averaged over 5 minutes so single slow probes do not dominate. A tunnel whose probe failed has no value here — it shows in the matrix as OUT.

panels.title: Stale AWG tunnels, master↔exit
panels.description: Exits whose oldest master handshake on awg0 is past 3 minutes. WireGuard re-handshakes every 2 minutes while the tunnel lives, so the healthy sawtooth stays under the line and draws nothing here.

panels.title: Exits silent at the master's AWG gate
panels.description: Tunnels where the master stopped hearing the exit's knock for 3+ minutes in this range (exit_initiated: the master answers an exit only after it knocks on its pinned port). Red = silent: the exit cannot reach the master. Empty = every exit kept knocking.

targets.expr: label_join((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_awg_exit_heard{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"})) and on(node, exit) (count_over_time((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_awg_exit_heard{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"}) == 0)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 3), "tunnel", " → ", "node", "exit") or on() (label_replace(vector(9), "tunnel", "every exit kept knocking", "", "") unless on() count(count_over_time((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_awg_exit_heard{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"}) == 0)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 3))

panels.title: Reserve-tier members that failed
panels.description: Reserve-tier exits whose warm probe failed for 3+ minutes in this range. These are the exits wg-best would fail over to if the primary tier died; red here means that failover would land on a dead exit. Empty = every reserve member answered.

targets.expr: label_join((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_standby_tier_member_usable{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"})) and on(node, exit) (count_over_time((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_standby_tier_member_usable{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"}) == 0)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 3), "tunnel", " → ", "node", "exit") or on() (label_replace(vector(9), "tunnel", "every reserve member answered", "", "") unless on() count(count_over_time((max by (node, exit) (wgfleet_agent_standby_tier_member_usable{node=~"$master",exit=~"$exit"}) == 0)[$__range:1m] @ end()) >= 3))

panels.title: Hold-outs per hour, master → exit
panels.description: Times a master's multi-destination probe took an exit out of the load balancer, per hour. Counts hold-outs too short for the timeline above (under 5 min) — the ones the console shows as 'out of rotation 3m'. Alert: WgfleetExitFlapping (2 in 6 h).

panels.title: REALITY bridge freezes per hour, exit → master
panels.description: Bridge sockets the exit's watchdog killed after 30 s of silence from that master's portal, per hour. Each one froze the traffic on it; the exit redials, so the bridge never reads as down. One master much higher than the others for the same exit points at that master's path. Alert: WgfleetRealityBridgeUnstable (over 3 an hour for an hour).

panels.title: Controller
panels.description: Build the controller reports. Agents' builds are in the table below.

panels.title: Fleet CA expires in
panels.description: Every node certificate chains to it; a lapsed CA cannot be repaired over the control plane.

panels.title: Manifest on disk
panels.description: Whether controller.yaml on disk matches what the controller loaded. 'unreadable' = the controller could not read it at all.

panels.title: Controller store
panels.description: 1 when the controller read its state store on the last scrape. While 0, every fleet-wide panel above is blind.

panels.title: Scanner list, IPv4 addresses by source
panels.description: What each source gave the last good list, largest copy across nodes. A source can publish half its list on a bad day; a drop here is the source, not the fleet.

panels.title: Scanner list in the kernel, per node (IPv4 entries)
panels.description: Entries in each node's as_blacklist set after merging. A node below the others is on an older list or failed to refresh; a node at zero with the feed on is open to scanners (fail-open). Masters show nothing while their feed is off.

panels.title: Checks failing now
panels.description: Health checks currently reporting 0, across every node in scope. Which ones is in the table below.

panels.title: Nodes failing, by check
panels.description: How many nodes are failing each check, over time. One row per check kind — that set is fixed by the agent code, so this panel stays readable however large the fleet gets. Green 'ok' = every node in scope passing; a coloured segment shows the number of nodes failing.

panels.title: Failures in this time range
panels.description: Every node/check pair that failed at least once in the selected range, and for how long. Sampled at 1-minute resolution, so a blip shorter than a minute still shows as 1.

defaults.noValue: ✓  no health check failed in this time range

panels.title: Client-path probes failing
panels.description: Probes the master runs from its OWN client through the full client path — interface, firewall, transparent proxy, exit — that currently fail. This is the one measurement that says whether a client works, as opposed to whether each component looks fine. Non-zero is a client-visible outage for that protocol.

panels.title: Client path, by probe
panels.description: Each end-to-end probe over time: ICMP through the direct route, the gateway and the mgmt overlay, TCP/443 and UDP/53 through the proxy. Read this to see WHICH protocol broke and when — a red UDP/53 with green TCP/443 is the return-path black hole, not an exit failure.

panels.title: Interception namespace
panels.description: Where the master is in the move of client interception into its own network namespace. `attached` is the steady state; `waiting` means the move is pending or was reverted and will be retried; `gave_up` means the revert allowance is spent and the node sits on the host path until someone looks.

panels.title: Path-guard drops (15m)
panels.description: Drops on `egress_path_guard` in the last 15 minutes — the chain that must never match. Anything above zero is a client packet that tried to leave by a path nobody chose, and the WgfleetGuardIsCatchingPackets alert fires on it.

panels.title: Client UDP black holes
panels.description: UDP ports this master holds a socket on that are NOT declared, so mihomo cannot open a transparent reply socket for them and client traffic to those ports gets no replies. Anything above zero is a silent outage for that port: requests leave, nothing returns.

targets.expr: count(wgfleet_agent_udp_return_socket == 0 and on(node, port) wgfleet_agent_udp_return_known == 0) or vector(0)

panels.title: UDP reply socket possible, by port
panels.description: 1 = a TPROXY reply socket can still be opened for that destination port; 0 = a socket this host already holds makes it impossible. Port 443 sitting at 0 is the client AmneziaWG interface holding it, which leaves client QUIC with no return path.

panels.title: Guard chain drops (15m)
panels.description: Packets each firewall guard chain dropped in the last 15 minutes. `egress_path_guard` asserts that no client packet leaves by a path nobody chose — it MUST stay at zero, and the alert pages on any value. `egress_leak_guard` catches stragglers that would otherwise leave un-NATed with a client address; a trickle is expected, a rising line means NAT is losing flows.

panels.title: mihomo error lines (5m)
panels.description: Error lines mihomo wrote about itself, per node, in the last 5 minutes. Deliberately unclassified: the signal is that the data plane is complaining at all. The master's line is the one that matters for clients; on exits it usually means a WireGuard device mihomo could not bring up.

panels.title: Active transport
panels.description: Which master↔exit transport each exit is currently routed over (awg / reality-xhttp). Switch it per node on its detail page.

panels.title: Standby transport usable
panels.description: Whether each dual-transport exit's INACTIVE transport — the one an operator would switch it onto — can actually reach the internet. Absent means never measured, which is not the same as healthy: an untested mihomo proxy reports alive=1 by default, so an unprobed standby shows a confident green on no evidence. The switch is an emergency move, made exactly when the active path is blocked.

defaults.noValue: no dual-transport exit has been measured yet

panels.title: Egress throughput per exit
panels.description: Measured egress bandwidth (passive live traffic, or an active probe on an idle link). The dashed line is the configured floor (250 KiB/s default); a sustained collapse below it auto-suspends the exit from the LB.

panels.title: Active egress method
panels.description: Which egress each exit is currently using (warp / direct). Differs from the preferred egress while failed over.

panels.title: Client-VLESS inbound down
panels.description: Masters whose client-facing VLESS/REALITY inbound self-check is failing. Non-zero means DPI-throttled clients can't fall back to the VLESS transport.

panels.title: VLESS clients issued
panels.description: Total VLESS/REALITY client credentials issued across selected masters.

panels.title: VLESS clients per master
panels.description: Issued VLESS/REALITY client count per master over time.

panels.title: Config drift (resources repaired)
panels.description: Resources the agent had to repair while the desired spec was unchanged — i.e. real drift or external tampering.

panels.title: mihomo restarts (30m) and self-heal throttle
panels.description: Restarts of mihomo's container in a trailing 30 minutes, from docker's own start time — every restart counts, whoever caused it — plus 1 while the agent's restart governor is refusing further self-heal restarts. A planner that restarts mihomo every pass knocks exits out of rotation within minutes, and the only record is a journal. A throttle is the same defect with the symptom muted.

panels.title: Probes that never succeeded
panels.description: Scheduled probes that have run at least once but have NEVER produced a result. Non-zero means the probe is dead while the node still reports Ready: it degrades to a default on failure, so nothing else surfaces it.

panels.title: Probes stale > 7d
panels.description: Probes that succeeded once but not in the last 7 days. Both probes run about daily, so this is a probe that started failing and kept the last-good value in force ever since.

panels.title: Time since last successful probe run
panels.description: Per node and probe: how long ago the probe last SUCCEEDED. A probe that has never succeeded shows an absurd age (measured from epoch) and colors red — that is the signature to look for. Rows appear only once a probe has actually run on that node.

panels.title: Nodes without host metrics
panels.description: Nodes the controller knows that have no node-exporter target up. Without the bootstrap's exporter only nodes whose hoster ships one have host metrics. A node here is one whose CPU, memory and disk are invisible — re-provision it, or check its prometheus-node-exporter unit.

panels.title: CPU busy
panels.description: Share of CPU not idle, per node. The overlay alone is CPU-bound on 1-vCPU boxes (ZeroTier is single-threaded), so a saturated master is a throughput ceiling on every client.

panels.title: Memory used
panels.description: 1 − MemAvailable/MemTotal. The OOM killer takes the largest process, which on a master is mihomo and every client connection with it.

panels.title: Root filesystem used
panels.description: Used share of /. Docker images, journald and the AS-blacklist cache live there; a full root stops the reconcile from writing config and the containers from restarting.

panels.title: Public interface traffic
panels.description: Bytes per second on each node's non-loopback, non-overlay, non-tunnel interfaces — the uplink. Receive is what clients send in (master) or the tunnel from the master (exit); transmit is what leaves for the internet.

panels.title: Load average (1m) per core
panels.description: 1-minute load divided by CPU count. Above 1 for long means work is queueing; on these small boxes that is usually WARP userspace crypto or a scanner storm hitting the firewall.
